A line through point B, $BP\parallel x$-axis, intersects the y-axis at point P. What is the area of $\triangle ABP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From (1) we have: $A(-2, 3)$, $B(3, -2)$,\\
since $BP\parallel x$-axis,\\
therefore, $BP=3$,\\
thus, the distance from point A to PB is $3-(-2)=5$,\\
hence, the area of $\triangle ABP$ is $\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 5=\boxed{\frac{15}{2}}$;

Reasoning: It is known that A=(-2,3) and B=(m,-2) are both on the hyperbola y=k2/x. Since A is on the hyperbola, k2=(-2)×3=-6. Since B is on the same hyperbola, m×(-2)=-6, so m=3, that is B=(3,-2). Because BP is horizontal and P is on the y-axis, P=(0,-2), and thus BP=3. The perpendicular distance from point A to the horizontal straight line PB is 3-(-2)=5. The area of triangle ABP is 1/2×3×5=15/2.
